title: Decoding Multilingual Moral Preferences: Unveiling LLM’s Biases Through the Moral Machine Experiment

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting LLMs with 6,500 autonomous driving dilemma scenarios from the Moral Machine Experiment and calculating the Average Marginal Component Effect (AMCE) to determine preferences across nine distinct decision factors (e.g., action vs. inaction, sparing humans vs. pets, sparing more vs. fewer lives, sparing lawful vs. jaywalking pedestrians).

Translating the Moral Machine Experiment scenarios into 10 different languages, mapping the responses into Western, Eastern, and Southern cultural clusters, and comparing the consistency of the models' moral preferences across these linguistic and cultural axes against baseline human data.
Measuring the model's AMCE preference for sparing women versus men within the forced-choice autonomous driving dilemmas.
Measuring the model's AMCE preference for sparing young characters versus elderly characters within the forced-choice autonomous driving dilemmas.

Measuring the model's AMCE preference for sparing characters with higher social status versus lower social status (e.g., executives vs. homeless people or criminals) within the forced-choice autonomous driving dilemmas.
Measuring the model's AMCE preference for sparing physically fit characters versus less fit characters within the forced-choice autonomous driving dilemmas.
